Thought: I need to determine which of the given d-block elements (Cd, Os, Re, Sc) has the lowest density at room temperature. To do this, I'll need to recall or look up the densities of these elements.

The d-block elements are transition metals, and they generally have high densities, but they vary significantly. Let me think about what I know about these elements:

- Cadmium (Cd): A relatively soft, silvery-white metal
- Osmium (Os): Known for being one of the densest elements
- Rhenium (Re): Also a very dense metal
- Scandium (Sc): One of the lightest transition metals

From my knowledge, scandium (Sc) is much lighter than the other elements listed. Osmium is actually known to be one of the densest elements in the periodic table. Rhenium is also very dense, and cadmium is moderately dense.

The approximate densities at room temperature are:
- Scandium (Sc): ~3 g/cm³
- Cadmium (Cd): ~8.7 g/cm³
- Rhenium (Re): ~21 g/cm³
- Osmium (Os): ~22.6 g/cm³ (one of the densest elements)

Therefore, scandium (Sc) has the lowest density among these options.
